sources.title: ICOBS 8.1.1R
sources.quote: An insurer must: (1) handle claims promptly and fairly; (2) provide reasonable guidance to help a policyholder make a claim and appropriate information on its progress; (3) not unreasonably reject a claim (including by terminating or avoiding a policy); and (4) settle claims promptly once settlement terms are agreed.
sources.note: The current handbook page was opened on 5 November 2026. The next numbered rule on that page is ICOBS 8.1.2. A point-in-time chapter view dated 21 January 2025 labels the same words ICOBS 8.1.1R. The current page's retrieved text did not print the characters 8.1.1 beside the first rule.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 22
sources.note: The article text is omitted. Textual amendment F1 says Chapter 3 Section 4A was substituted for Article 22, in force on 5 February 2026, by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 section 80(1) and S.I. 2026/82 regulation 2(j).

sources.title: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 section 80
sources.quote: For the purposes of Articles 22B and 22C— (a) a decision is based solely on automated processing if there is no meaningful human involvement in the taking of the decision, and (b) a decision is a significant decision, in relation to a data subject, if— (i) it produces a legal effect for the data subject, or (ii) it has a similarly significant effect for the data subject.
sources.note: Section 80(1) substitutes Articles 22A to 22D for Article 22. The page says there are no known outstanding effects. Commencement: in force at Royal Assent for specified purposes, and on 5 February 2026 in so far as not already in force, by S.I. 2026/82 regulation 2(j).

sources.title: FCA AI in financial services: good practice and areas for improvement
sources.quote: One firm assessed AI-generated claims information against a structured set of criteria, including completeness, faithfulness to source information, conciseness, adequacy of reasoning, and safety. It combined checks by staff with an automated assessment, including LLM-as-a-judge.
sources.note: Published 19 October 2026. Last updated 20 October 2026. Case study K is under section 3.2 Monitoring and oversight. The glossary defines LLM-as-a-judge as using one large language model to assess the output of another AI system. This starter's checker is deterministic. It is not that judge.

sources.title: Microsoft Foundry RAG evaluators
sources.quote: Groundedness measures how well the generated response aligns with the given context without fabricating content. Groundedness Pro is marked preview.
sources.note: The page says Groundedness returns pass or fail from a 1 to 5 scale, with a default pass threshold of 3. This starter does not use that scale and does not call the evaluator. Response Completeness is marked preview on the same page.

automated_decision_note: UK GDPR Article 22 was substituted by Articles 22A to 22D. A decline can be a significant decision where it produces a legal effect or a similarly significant effect, and it is based solely on automated processing where there is no meaningful human involvement. This draft does not take that decision. Whether a particular decline meets the test is for the data protection officer.
limitations: This draft does not accept, decline, or settle a claim.
It does not tell the customer anything. There is no customer message.
It does not write to a claims system, including after a handler records a class.
An inconsistency line is a prompt for a person to check. It is not a finding and it is not a statement about the policyholder's conduct.
A coverage pointer is a quote. It is not a statement that the loss is or is not within the policy.
The class is a proposal until a claims handler records one. Recording a class is not an outcome.
The scorecard is a deterministic checker. It is not an LLM-as-a-judge and it is not a Microsoft Foundry score. Thresholds are not approved.
A score under a draft threshold asks a person to look. It does not decline the claim.
Conciseness and adequacy of reasoning, named in the FCA case study, are not scored.
Document inventory and UK identifier spans come from Experiment 12 and Experiment 08. A file with an identifier is not quoted. The text is not anonymised.
Faithfulness comes from Experiment 29. This module does not re-implement that checker.
Only labelled lines and one policy line are quoted. Other sentences in the file are not extracted.
